name: Glisper Connector
author: glisper

sections.description:
Glisper shows how AI assistants and search engines describe your business, and finds what to fix on your website. Glisper Connector lets Glisper read your published pages and apply the fixes you approve in Glisper, so you do not have to copy each one into WordPress by hand.

What it does

  • Reads your published pages and posts (titles, headings, word counts, SEO titles and meta descriptions) and basic site facts, such as your site name, theme, SEO plugin and WordPress version.
  • Applies only the exact changes you approve in Glisper, where you see the current and the new text first:
    • a page’s SEO title or meta description, saved in Yoast SEO, Rank Math, SEOPress or The SEO Framework when one of them is active, or printed by this plugin when none is;
    • a page’s main heading, on pages built with the block editor;
    • a link to an address that redirects, pointed at its final address;
    • your organization’s name and website as structured data, when no SEO plugin prints organization markup;
    • a new draft post, which is never published.
  • Each change is saved only if the field still has the value you saw in Glisper, so a newer edit is never overwritten, and every change can be restored from Glisper.

What it never does

It never publishes anything, deletes your content, or changes users, plugins, themes, settings or code. It creates no WordPress user, role or Application Password: Glisper connects with a key that works only on this plugin’s own endpoints, and your site keeps only a fingerprint of it. Disconnect in Glisper or deactivate the plugin to delete the key at any time.

Requirements

  • A Glisper account with a workspace for this website. Applying fixes needs a Glisper plan that includes fixes.
  • A single-site WordPress installation served over HTTPS.

External services

This plugin connects your site to Glisper, a service at glisper.app, so that Glisper can read your published pages and apply the changes you approve. It contacts Glisper only in the steps below, all started by an administrator.

  • Approving. When you click Approve and connect to Glisper on Tools > Glisper, your browser opens the Glisper app (app.glisper.app) with this site’s address and a one-time state value. There you sign in and choose the workspace, and Glisper sends your browser back to Tools > Glisper with a one-time connect code. Nothing is sent from your server in this step.
  • Finishing. The plugin then asks Glisper’s API (api.glisper.app) to confirm the code for this site, sending the request’s ID and the code. Once Glisper confirms it, the plugin creates a random key, keeps only its SHA-256 fingerprint, and sends the key, with the request’s ID and code, to Glisper’s API. Glisper stores it encrypted and sends it with each call to this plugin’s own endpoints; nothing else on your site accepts it.
  • Afterwards, Glisper calls your site; this plugin sends nothing on its own. Glisper reads your published, public posts and pages (ID, type, address, title, last-modified time, headings, editor type, word count, a fingerprint of the content, SEO title and meta description, and how often a given link address appears in a page) and site facts (WordPress, PHP and plugin versions, site name and address, whether a tagline is set, whether search engines are discouraged, which pages are the homepage and posts page, permalink structure, language, public post types, theme, active SEO plugin, and the organization markup this plugin saved). It also sends the changes you approved, and the plugin answers with each change’s result.

Nothing else is sent: no visitor data, comments, orders, user accounts or passwords, and no other settings.

  • Glisper Terms of Service: https://app.glisper.app/terms
  • Glisper Privacy Policy: https://app.glisper.app/privacy
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, go to Plugins > Add New, search for “Glisper Connector”, then install and activate it. Or click Connect WordPress on Glisper’s Integrations page: it takes you to this plugin in your WordPress admin.
  2. The plugin opens Tools > Glisper. Check what Glisper may read and change, then click Approve and connect to Glisper.
  3. Sign in to Glisper if asked and choose your workspace. You come straight back, the connection finishes, and Glisper shows your site as connected.

To connect a development or staging site to another Glisper address, define GLISPER_API_URL and GLISPER_APP_URL in wp-config.php before the plugin loads.
sections.faq:
Do I need a Glisper account?

Yes. The plugin only connects your site to your Glisper workspace; Glisper finds the fixes and shows them to you for approval. You can create an account at https://app.glisper.app/signup.

Does it work with my SEO plugin?

Yes, with Yoast SEO, Rank Math, SEOPress and The SEO Framework: Glisper saves the title and description in that plugin’s own fields for the page, so your SEO plugin keeps printing them and shows them in its editor panel. All in One SEO keeps its values in its own table, so those changes stay manual. Without an SEO plugin, this plugin prints the title and description Glisper saved.

Can I undo a change?

Yes. Every applied change can be restored from Glisper, and only where nobody has edited that field since.

Does Glisper get a WordPress login?

No. The plugin creates no WordPress user, role or Application Password, and no WordPress password is shared with Glisper. Glisper connects with a random key that only this plugin’s own endpoints accept, and your site keeps only a fingerprint of it.

What happens when I deactivate or delete the plugin?

Deactivating deletes Glisper’s key, so Glisper can no longer read or change anything. Titles and descriptions it saved stay with your pages: an SEO plugin keeps showing them, and without one they stop showing until the plugin is active again. Deleting the plugin also removes its settings.

Does it support multisite?

Not yet. It needs a single-site installation. On a multisite network it activates but does nothing, and the Plugins screen says so.
sections.changelog:
0.8.1

  • Glisper moved to glisper.app. The plugin now uses api.glisper.app and app.glisper.app; the old addresses keep working.

0.8.0

  • Connecting takes one approval: Approve and connect to Glisper opens Glisper to choose the workspace and finishes when you come back. The plugin no longer accepts connection requests from outside, so it has no public endpoint.
  • Glisper connects with a key that only this plugin’s own endpoints accept. The plugin no longer creates a WordPress user or an Application Password, so sites with Application Passwords turned off can connect too. A site connected with an earlier version connects again once.
  • Glisper’s requests and this plugin’s answers are never stored by a page cache or CDN.
  • Activating on a multisite network no longer stops with an error: the plugin does nothing there and says so on the Plugins screen.
  • Tools > Glisper no longer causes a PHP warning when debugging is on.
  • A new main heading with a price in it (“from $199”) is saved exactly as approved.
  • The readme and the approval page list exactly what Glisper reads.

0.7.0

  • Connect from the plugin’s own page (Tools > Glisper), so a copy installed from WordPress.org needs no download.
  • Glisper’s addresses are built in. A development or staging site can set GLISPER_API_URL and GLISPER_APP_URL in wp-config.php.
  • Deactivating the plugin always completes; it revokes Glisper’s access first.
  • Translatable admin text.

0.6.0

  • Titles and descriptions are saved in Yoast SEO, Rank Math, SEOPress or The SEO Framework when one of them is active.
